headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users, such as data centers, to bear more of the costs for grid infrastructure and capacity, thereby protecting residential ratepayers from these expenses.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, Governor Spanberger, Senator Louise Lucas, Dominion Energy (with amendments)
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users (initially, before amendments)
news_headline: SCC Orders Data Centers to Pay for Transmission Infrastructure
news_summary: Following Governor Spanberger's urging, the State Corporation Commission (SCC) mandated data centers cover the full cost of their dedicated transmission infrastructure, saving Virginia ratepayers hundreds of millions. This decision aligns with legislative efforts to shift energy costs to high-demand users, preventing residential customers from bearing these expenses.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates waterworks operators to report categorized monthly water sales, including specific data center consumption, to enhance transparency and aid state water supply planning.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, transparency advocates, State Sen. Kannan Srinivasan (D–Loudoun), Virginia Department of Environmental Quality
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden/scrutiny)
news_headline: Virginia Data Centers Face New Water Use Reporting Rules
news_summary: New regulations, effective January 2027, require waterworks operators to categorize and report monthly water sales, specifically including data center consumption. This aims to increase transparency and assist the Department of Environmental Quality in water supply planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high-energy-use facilities, including noise studies near residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups, Del. Thomas (sponsor), Governor Spanberger
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Siting, Noise Studies
news_summary: Under HB 153, high-energy-use facilities like data centers must undergo site assessments, including noise studies for nearby homes and schools. Localities can also require assessments of impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites before approval.
